messages.subject: zero-inflated poisson model
parts:
Dear all,

We are doing some research by using the nimble code.
Sometimes it can run. But sometimes it faces some error.
(R encounter fatal error. session terminate....)
(We are not sure why sometime can run and sometimes cannot run it.)
(It can show the progress bar, so we think our code it corrects and have enough computer memory.)
Our computer has 64G memory. 

I also attached our code.
Can someone help us to check the error?

MainCode <- nimbleCode({
  
  for(s in 1:S){    
     
    for(j in 1:Q){
      Y[s,j] ~ dZIP(lambda[s,j], zeroProb = p.ZIP[s])             
      lambda[s,j] <- #N[s]*
                    exp(b[s, 1] * x1[j] +
                                b[s, 2] * x2[j] + b[s, 3] * x3[j] + b[s, 4] * x4[j] +
                                b[s, 5] * x5[j] + b[s, 6] * x6[j])
    }
    
    ##Cluster for beta (b) and p.ZIP 
    b[s, 1:6] <- bm[latent[s], 1:6]
    p.ZIP[s] <- pm[latent[s]]         
    latent[s] ~ dcat(pi[1:M])
  }
  
  ### clustered coefficients: MFM ###
  for (i in 1:M) {
    r[i] ~ dexp(rate = lambda.MFM)
  }
  rcumsum[1:M] <- Rcumsum(r[1:M])
  pik[1:(M+1)] <- piFun(r = r[1:M], rcumsum = rcumsum[1:M])
  pi[1:M] <- pik[1:M]
  K <- pik[M+1]
  
  #lambda.MFM ~ dunif(0, 100)
  lambda.MFM ~ dlnorm(0, varlog = 1)
  
  for (k in 1:M) {
    bm[k, 1:6] ~ dmnorm(mu_bm[1:6], cov = var_bm[1:6, 1:6])  
    #pm[k] ~ dnorm(mu_pm, tau = tau_pm) 
    pm[k] ~ dunif(0,1)
  }
  
})

Best,
Hou-Cheng

messages.subject: Re: zero-inflated poisson model
parts:
hi Hou-Cheng,

It looks like this is producing a segmentation fault, which occurs when NIMBLE's auto-generated C++ code tries to write to some memory address beyond the length of a vector.

In the code that you shared with me in a separate email, I see this:

piFun <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(r = double(1), rcumsum = double(1)) {
    rlength <- length(r)
    prob <- rep(0, rlength)
    i <- 1
    while (rcumsum[i] < 1) {
      prob[i] <- r[i]
      i <- i + 1
    }
    prob[i] <- 1 - sum(r[1:(i-1)])
    returnType(double(1))
    return(c(prob,i))
  }
)

The danger in having a while loop like this is that the code could end up in a situation, depending on the values in 'r', that the code tries to access elements of 
r and of rcumsum beyond the extent of those vectors, e.g., rcumsum[rlength+1], and trying to modify prob[i] for i > rlength.  I see in your code that the elements of 
r are being generated from rexp(), which doesn't constrain the elements to add to 1 for a fixed number of elements. So I think this is arising only sometimes in
the execution of your code, because it is rare that the code goes beyond the extent of the vector.

So you'll need to add some checking to your piFun to make sure that you never go beyond the length of the vectors.

Side note: even if 'r' were created in such a way that the elements add to 1, because of the limited precision of double-precision floating point numbers,
it would still be possible that rcumsum[rlength] could be a bit less than one numerically, such that this problem could still arise.
